archetype.name: Lost Season (collapse after a winning year)
archetype.definition: Memphis followed a 48-34 season by dropping to 25-57 and last in the Southwest, with a defense that leaked and a rotation full of players still finding their level.

report.headline: A 48-win team's follow-up collapsed into eight straight losses, last in the Southwest

recap.finish: 25-57, fifth in the Southwest; missed the postseason
recap.body:
This was a team that played fast and shot a lot of threes but could not defend or finish possessions on its own glass. Its Net Rtg of -5.9 ranked 24th, with the offense 24th (112.9 ORtg) and the defense 23rd (118.8 DRtg). The fall from last year is the story. The 2024-25 team went 48-34 with the sixth-best offense, a 117.7 ORtg and a +4.7 Net Rtg. This one lost ground on both ends and slid to 26th of 30 on the site's Teams tab.

The first two months gave no warning of what came later. Memphis was 15-18 at the end of December after a 6-6 month in which it outscored opponents, 120.25 to 116.58 a game. Then the season gave way. January went 3-11, February 4-7, March 3-14 with opponents scoring 124.29 a game, and April 0-7 at 135.14 allowed. Its longest winning streak all year was three games. The year closed with a one-point win over Chicago on March 28 and then eight straight losses, the season's longest skid. Over the last 10 games the defense gave up 132 a game, and over the last five 137.6, including a 147-101 loss in Utah.

The record isn't a fluke of close games. W vs Pt Diff was -2, and the -493 differential implies 27 wins, so Memphis was only a couple of wins worse than its margin. The causes are structural. Opponents shot a 56.2 eFG % (26th), and the Grizzlies grabbed only 70.9% of available defensive rebounds (29th), so stops often became second chances. Power forwards did the most damage: they scored more above their own averages against Memphis than against any other defense. The one thing the defense did well was force turnovers; its Opp TOV % of 13.3 ranked 8th. On offense, a 43.6 3PA Rate (10th) paired with 35.3% shooting from deep (22nd) meant volume without payoff.

The group grades match that picture: backcourt C-, frontcourt C, wings F. The wing grade rests on two players with fewer than 500 listed minutes between them, and the floor collapsed with both. Tyler Burton's On-Off was -17.7 and Dariq Whitehead's -18.6. Cam Spencer was the best player on the roster: 14th of 144 on his tab, a 64.9 TS %, 400 assists and 5.3 Win Shares. Cedric Coward (30th, +10.1 On-Off) and Santi Aldama (20th of 93, but only 43 games) were the other positives. Walter Clayton (52.3 TS %, -4.3 BPM) and Jaylen Wells (-3.1 BPM) took heavy minutes without producing. Zach Edey played 11 games and posted a +25.4 On-Off, a number too small to build on but too loud to ignore.

The franchise has been here before. The 2023-24 team went 27-55 and was followed by a 48-win season. Nothing in this sheet says that will repeat, but it does show that this year's bottom is about as deep as that one, not deeper.

highlights.title: Cam Spencer ran the offense well
highlights.body: Spencer combined a 64.9 TS % with 400 assists and led the listed roster with 5.3 Win Shares, ranking 14th of 144 at his position. He did it at a modest 17.2 USG %, so his value came from efficiency and playmaking rather than volume. Of everyone on the roster, his profile looks the most repeatable.

highlights.title: Coward and Aldama moved the needle
highlights.body: Cedric Coward posted a +10.1 On-Off across 1,598 minutes while scoring 843 points and pulling 364 rebounds. Aldama graded 20th of 93 at his position with a positive BPM. Aldama only managed 43 games, though, and how much of the frontcourt's C grade he carried depends on whether he stays available.

highlights.title: Defense forced turnovers
highlights.body: Opponents turned it over at a 13.3 Opp TOV % rate, 8th in the league and above the league average. It was the one defensive habit that held up while everything else gave way. It is a usable base if the half-court defense and rebounding improve.

lowlights.title: Defense and defensive glass gave way
lowlights.body: Opponents shot a 56.2 eFG % (26th), and Memphis secured only 70.9% of available defensive rebounds (29th). That is well below both the league and its own 2024-25 level. Power forwards exceeded their own averages against this defense more than against any other team. This was the core reason the team lost by margin, and it was not bad luck.

lowlights.title: A season-ending freefall
lowlights.body: After sitting at 15-18 at the end of December, Memphis won only a handful of games the rest of the way. It went 3-14 in March and 0-7 in April. The last 10 games came at a -20.4 margin a game with 132 allowed, far worse than the season-long defense. The team didn't drift to the bottom; it stopped competing late.

lowlights.title: No wing group to speak of
lowlights.body: The wings graded F, carried by two small forwards who barely played and were badly negative when they did: Burton at -17.7 and Whitehead at -18.6 On-Off. The guards and power forwards absorbed those minutes. The roster needs a real wing.

arc.note: Memphis hovered near .500 through December at 15-18, then lost steadily from January on. It finished 0-7 in April and closed on eight straight losses.

recap.nextYear: The numbers that carry forward are Spencer's efficient playmaking, Coward's strong On-Off and Aldama's quality when healthy. Edey's 11 games at a +25.4 On-Off and 66.9 TS % are a tantalizing but tiny sample. Luck explains almost none of the 25 wins: the margin implied 27, so the gap to respectability is real. The biggest fixes are defensive rebounding and the wing spot, which graded F with almost no minutes from real wings. The backcourt also needs more from Clayton and Wells, who logged big minutes with negative BPMs. The 2023-24 to 2024-25 swing shows this franchise has jumped from a near-identical record before. But this sheet's roster gives no basis for assuming it will, beyond better health and growth from its young core.

confidence.note: Full 82-game season with a clear trend; individual small samples (Edey, the wings) are flagged as such.
